meaning: (?) the son of Avenel (?); origin queried by the author
author_comment: Always without prefix in the Hundred Rolls, whose instances are generally in the neighbourhood of co. Camb. Mr. Lower suggests a local origin from Avenelles, in the department of Eure. This is quite possible; one thing seems quite certain, the chief modern variant is Averill or Averell. Any one who has studied the corruptions undergone by surnames will feel no surprise at this.
source: Hundred Rolls, 1273

meaning: the son of ---- (?); origin uncertain, perhaps Atkinson
author_comment: This Lancashire and Cheshire surname has clearly no connexion with Axton (q.v.). It is a patronymic formed like Jaxon, Dixon, Dix, or Cox, which represent Jackson, Dickson, Dicks, or Cocks. I can but suggest that it is Atkinson, which in my part of Lancashire (Furness) is invariably pronounced Atkison or Akison; v. Atkinson.
source: Wills at Chester, 1545-1620 (Lancashire and Cheshire Record Society), p. 1
